chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who died and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and had not made a will regarding it; should it be performed on his behalf? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَتُقْضَى: Should it be made up/performed on behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hajj for a Muslim who died without having performed it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Hajj al-Islam (the first obligatory pilgrimage) remains a debt upon the deceased even without a specific bequest, allowing heirs to fulfill it from the estate. This ruling underscores the concept of 'Hajj al-Dayn' (debt Hajj) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from voluntary supererogatory pilgrimages and emphasizing the continuity of religious duties after death.
